description: A single sleepy calf curled in a patch of afternoon sun, its oversized ears twitching at flies, lashes fluttering as it drifts in and out of a warm nap on a bed of golden hay.

Two baby goats perched on a mossy stone wall, one boldly leaning forward with ears fanned wide and curious eyes, the other tucked shyly behind, peeking just enough to watch everything happening in the yard below.

Three fluffy ducklings and their mother waddling single-file through a sun-dappled garden path, the smallest one perpetually two steps behind, stumbling over its own feet but determinedly keeping pace, bill open in silent protest.

A small cluster of piglets — four of them, rosy and round — rooting through a clover patch with absolute focus, snouts to the earth, tiny curled tails wiggling furiously, completely unbothered by the world.

A gathering of seven animals at the gate near feeding time: two lambs pressing their woolly heads through the fence slats, a pair of chicks scrambling between everyone's feet, an old farm dog sitting patiently in the middle, and two kittens batting at the dog's wagging tail as if it were invented purely for their entertainment.

A gentle pony standing at a cottage window, breath fogging the glass, soft nose nearly touching the pane — three fluffy chicks have followed it right up and are now clustered at its hooves, peering upward at their own fuzzy reflections with tremendous seriousness.

Six baby rabbits tumbling out of a garden bed like a small, velvet avalanche — ears too large, legs not entirely coordinated — chasing each other through the lettuce rows while a sleepy farm cat observes from a nearby post with the weary patience of someone who has seen it all before.

An improbable parade trailing across the yard: twelve animals at least — four piglets, two skipping lambs, a calf still figuring out its legs, three chicks riding improbably on the calf's back, two ducklings waddling sideways, a puppy spinning circles around all of them, and one utterly unbothered rooster leading the procession as though this is perfectly normal and always has been.

A hay loft scene of generous sleepiness: two kittens kneaded into each other like bread dough, a lamb tucked against a dozing farm dog, three chicks nestled into the warmth between them, everyone breathing slowly in the amber afternoon light filtering through the barn slats.

Four baby goats playing a game with no apparent rules — leaping off a low fence, bouncing off each other, spinning mid-air for the sheer joy of it, landing on unsteady legs, and immediately running back to the start to do it all again with escalating enthusiasm.
A single drowsy calf curled up in a nest of golden hay, chin resting on its own knees, long eyelashes fluttering as it drifts in and out of a gentle afternoon nap.
Two baby goats perched on a mossy stone wall, one nudging the other with a tiny horn, both teetering and giggling in that wordless goat way, ears flopping with every bump.

Three ducklings waddling single-file through a cottage garden, investigating every dewdrop on every leaf, the smallest one persistently veering off-path to chase a cabbage-white butterfly before waddling frantically back to catch up.

A plump tabby farm cat sprawled across a sun-warmed windowsill while two kittens bat at the dangling curtain hem below her, completely unbothered by their chaos, tail swishing once in mild disapproval.

Four piglets crowding the fence at feeding time, snouts pressed between the slats, tiny curly tails spinning in frantic circles, each one absolutely convinced it is the hungriest animal that has ever lived.

A golden retriever farm dog trots through the yard trailed by six fluffy chicks who have collectively decided she is their mother, peeping urgently whenever she gets more than two steps ahead, and she has simply accepted this responsibility with great dignity.

Seven animals gathered at the barn door in the soft morning light — a patient old pony, two lambs leaning against her legs, a rooster strutting importantly across the threshold, and three kittens draped over the half-door, all waiting for breakfast with varying degrees of composure.

Six ducklings and two baby rabbits have somehow ended up sharing the same shallow mud puddle, splashing and hopping with the combined energy of creatures who have never once considered consequences, while a sleepy sheepdog watches from the shade with one eye half open.

An inexplicable assembly of animals has formed in the vegetable garden — four piglets rooting cheerfully through the carrot bed, two baby goats balancing on the raised planter, a lamb eating something it definitely should not, five chicks sprinting in every direction, a kitten riding the lamb's back with enormous confidence, and one very smug rooster overseeing all of it from atop the scarecrow post.

Twelve animals somehow squeezed into the farmhouse mudroom — three puppies tumbling over a pile of boots, two ducklings waddling across the flagstone floor leaving tiny wet prints, a calf with its enormous head through the door looking hopeful, four kittens investigating coat pockets, a bunny thumping on the welcome mat, and a single very confused piglet who took a wrong turn and has no idea how it got here but seems pleased regardless.
A single sleepy calf curled up in a nest of golden hay, chin resting on folded legs, big brown eyes blinking slowly as it drifts in and out of a gentle afternoon nap.
Two fluffy bunnies nose-to-nose in a patch of clover, one nudging the other with persistent curiosity while the second sits perfectly still, pretending not to notice.

Three baby goats in the garden — one boldly chewing on a sunflower stem, one frozen mid-leap with all four hooves off the ground, and one shy little kid peering out from behind a watering can with enormous eyes.

A mama duck leading four fluffy ducklings single-file along the edge of a puddle, each duckling waddling with tremendous personal confidence, the last one perpetually three steps behind and hurrying to catch up.
Four piglets tumbling around a mud puddle — two wrestling enthusiastically, one sitting apart looking profoundly dignified, and one trotting in determined circles for reasons known only to itself.
A single drowsy calf curled up in a nest of golden hay, chin resting on its own knees, eyes blinking slowly as afternoon light spills across its soft brown coat.
Two tiny ducklings waddling in determined single file through a garden path, pausing every few steps to peer under a leaf with enormous curiosity, then rushing to catch up to each other.

Three baby goats taking turns leaping off a mossy stone wall — one launches with gleeful abandon, one watches with skeptical hesitation, and the third has already wandered off to nibble the garden gate.
A plump mama duck trailed by four fuzzy ducklings crossing a sun-warmed flagstone path, the last little one sprinting frantically on stubby legs to close a widening gap, cheeping the whole way.

A sleepy farm cat draped over a fence rail with two kittens tumbling underneath it — one kitten swatting at the cat's dangling tail while the other has its head stuffed entirely inside an empty flower pot.

Seven animals gathered at the barn door as feeding time approaches — a pair of lambs pressing their noses eagerly through the slats, four chicks scratching at the ground in concentrated circles, and one very round piglet sitting perfectly still in the center of everything as if presiding over the whole affair.

Six piglets and a pair of puppies have launched a full cooperative investigation of the vegetable garden — two piglets tunnel under a cabbage leaf, three puppies chase each other between the bean rows, one piglet stands very still in the middle looking genuinely surprised to be there, and the last puppy is already asleep under the wheelbarrow.

A gentle old pony stands in the paddock while six assorted admirers cluster around it — two lambs pressed against its warm flank, three chicks perched along the fence rail watching with intense focus, and one small kitten who has somehow climbed onto the pony's broad back and gone completely to sleep.

Twelve animals have collectively escaped into the cottage garden and nobody is handling it well — four ducklings are in the birdbath, three piglets are rooting through the lavender with tremendous enthusiasm, two baby goats are standing on the garden bench looking smug, a lamb is pressing its entire face against the kitchen window, a kitten has claimed the top of the fence post, and one overwhelmed puppy sits in the middle of it all spinning in slow circles.

An improbable procession has formed behind a single small bucket — two calves jostling for the front position, four bunnies hopping in loose formation behind them, three chicks weaving between everyone's feet causing constant near-disasters, two puppies barking at the chicks instead of following, a piglet who joined purely out of social pressure, and a rooster bringing up the rear with the grave dignity of someone who absolutely started this whole thing.
A single sleepy calf curled up in a nest of golden hay, its big brown eyes half-closed, tail flicking lazily, one velvety ear twitching at a passing fly.

Two tiny kittens perched on a mossy stone wall, peering wide-eyed through a cottage window, their small paws pressed flat against the glass, breath fogging little circles as they watch curiously inside.
A trio of ducklings waddling single-file through a vegetable garden, peeping softly, each one stopping to peck hopefully at a strawberry before tumbling forward to catch up with the leader.

Four baby goats bouncing and leaping across a gentle hillside, entirely delighted with themselves — one hops sideways for no reason, another tries to climb a tilted fence post, two butt heads gently and then stare at each other in mild surprise.
A fluffy farm dog dozing in a sun-warmed doorway while three puppies clamber over her belly, chewing on her ears and tumbling into each other, utterly ignoring her long-suffering sighs.

A cheerful gathering at the morning feeding bucket — six chicks darting between boots, two piglets shouldering each other for position, a lamb pressing its whole face hopefully against a knee, and a duckling that wandered into the wrong crowd entirely and seems unbothered about it.

Seven baby rabbits spilling out of a clover patch at dusk, ears swiveling in every direction, some pausing with noses twitching furiously, the boldest ones hopping right up to sniff at shoelaces while the shyest peers from the safety of a tall dandelion.

A gentle parade trailing down a country lane — two lambs trotting eagerly ahead, a curious calf lumbering alongside, four chicks sprinting to keep pace, and a sleepy-faced pony bringing up the rear at its own unhurried, swaying pace.

An absolute menagerie has gathered in the yard for no clear reason — four piglets rooting through a flower pot, three ducklings chasing a butterfly in circles, two kittens riding a patient old sheep like a very fluffy boat, a goat kid balanced triumphantly on a wheelbarrow, a pair of puppies wrestling in a puddle, and one extremely smug rooster surveying the whole disaster from a fence post.

Somehow twelve animals have crowded onto the cottage porch — piglets, bunnies, chicks, a calf, ducklings, a very confused baby goat, and two kittens sitting atop a dozing farm dog — all pressing warmly together in a wriggling, peeping, nuzzling heap as if someone promised them something wonderful was about to happen inside.
A single sleepy calf curled up in a golden nest of hay, its big brown eyes blinking slowly, one velvet ear twitching at a passing fly, too drowsy to bother moving.
Two fluffy kittens pressed nose-to-nose on a sun-warmed windowsill, one pawing lazily at the other's ear, both watching the farmyard outside with half-lidded, curious eyes.

Three spotted piglets rooting enthusiastically through a vegetable garden, snouts deep in the soil, bumping each other out of the way and squealing softly with competitive delight over every earthworm they uncover.
A gentle farm dog trotting through the meadow with four fluffy ducklings waddling in a determined line behind it, convinced it is their mother, peeping loudly whenever it moves too fast.

A lively cluster of chicks and two baby goats sharing a sunny patch of yard — the chicks darting between the goats' legs chasing dandelion seeds while the baby goats hop sideways at each flutter of wings, too playful to settle but too charmed to wander away.

A pair of lambs and a small round bunny grazing side by side in the afternoon clover, the bunny occasionally thumping a back foot and startling both lambs into a brief, bouncy gallop before all three drift calmly back together.

Six ducklings and a mother duck crossing a muddy puddle in single file, the last duckling consistently slipping sideways off the path, waddling furiously to catch up, peeping in indignant protest while its siblings paddle ahead without a backward glance.

A shaggy pony standing patiently in a field while seven chicks peck contentedly around its hooves, one brave chick having claimed the pony's forelock as a napping spot, small and puffed up like a tiny sun, while the pony exhales very gently so as not to disturb it.

An overwhelming parade of farm animals converging on the barn at feeding time — four piglets skidding on wet grass, three lambs bouncing shoulder-to-shoulder, two kittens riding a wandering goat who has stolen a carrot, a puppy spinning in confused circles, five chicks underfoot everywhere at once, and a lone duck standing in the middle of it all looking deeply unimpressed.

Twelve animals in a sun-drenched farmyard with no clear authority in charge — ducklings trying to climb into a bucket, a calf peering through the kitchen window with enormous hopeful eyes, piglets tangled in a row of hanging laundry, baby rabbits and kittens tumbling over each other in the herb patch, two baby goats attempting to headbutt a watering can, and a rooster strutting through it all with the misplaced confidence of someone who believes he is responsible for the sun rising.
A single sleepy calf curled up in a nest of golden hay, its oversized ears twitching at a passing fly, one eye half-open as if deciding whether getting up is truly worth the effort.
Two baby goats perched on a mossy stone wall, bumping heads and bouncing back with obvious delight, their stubby little tails wiggling furiously every time they make contact.

A small flock of ducklings — four of them, lemon-yellow and impossibly round — waddling single-file through tall grass, the last one always a half-step behind, peeping urgently to keep up with the group.

Three piglets rooting happily through a muddy garden patch, snouts working overtime, occasionally glancing up with bright curious eyes before diving back in with tremendous enthusiasm and absolutely no apology for the mess.

A pair of kittens and two fluffy bunnies sharing a sunny patch of porch in an unlikely afternoon truce — the kittens grooming each other lazily, the bunnies twitching their noses at every breeze, all four radiating collective contentment.

A cheerful gathering of seven chicks pecking around the feet of a patient old hen, each one chasing the same crumb in rotating turns, scattering dramatically at a falling leaf and then rushing back together in a tight, peeping huddle.

Six lambs racing across a clover field at dusk for absolutely no reason, leaping sideways in that sudden joyful way lambs do, their fluffy white forms bouncing like popcorn while a mildly exasperated sheep watches from the fence.

A farm dog puppy — wide paws, floppy ears — tumbling through a cluster of five ducklings near the pond, completely overwhelmed by their waddling fearlessness, tail spinning like a propeller as the ducklings refuse to scatter and instead investigate his nose.

An inexplicable congregation of twelve animals has appeared at the cottage door: four piglets pressing their snouts to the glass, two ducklings somehow already inside on the mat, three baby goats climbing the window box, a calf standing in the flower bed looking guilty, and two kittens supervising the entire situation from the roof of the letterbox with great self-importance.

Feeding time has escalated completely beyond reason — a rooster is shouting announcements from the fence post, eight chicks are rioting underfoot, three lambs have stolen an entire bucket and are running with it, two puppies are chasing the lambs, a pair of geese are honking directions no one asked for, and somewhere in the middle of it all a single tiny duckling is napping, unbothered, in a feed bowl.
A single drowsy calf curled up in a patch of afternoon sunlight, chin resting on a tuft of hay, eyelids heavy, occasionally flicking one ear at a passing fly with the most profound reluctance.
Two baby goats perched on a mossy stone wall, wobbling with excited little hops, their tiny hooves skittering as they butt heads gently and then look absolutely startled by what they have done.

Three ducklings waddling single-file through a cottage garden, each one determinedly following the next, occasionally veering into a lavender bush and emerging with petals stuck to their fuzzy heads, entirely unbothered.

A plump mama rabbit and four round baby bunnies tucked into the tall grass at the meadow edge — the babies twitching their noses furiously at everything, one boldly creeping forward to investigate a dandelion before losing its nerve and bolting back.

Four piglets rooting cheerfully along the garden fence, their curly tails spinning with enthusiasm, one persistently trying to squeeze its round belly through a gap it absolutely will not fit through, the others cheering it on by piling up behind.

A gathering of seven animals at the afternoon feed — two lambs butting shoulders for position, three chicks darting between bigger feet and snatching crumbs, a sleepy farm cat watching from a fence post with supreme disinterest, and a puppy bounding in circles around the whole group, delighted to have been invited.

Six kittens and two puppies tumbling through a barn doorway in a rolling, squeaking knot — kittens pouncing on puppy ears, puppies flopping over in surrender, everyone pausing briefly to stare at a moth and then immediately forgetting what they were doing.

A gentle old farm dog ambling through the orchard trailed by seven ducklings who have decided she is their mother — she glances back at them with a long-suffering sigh and keeps walking, the ducklings waddling faster with urgent little quacks to keep up.

An improbable parade of twelve animals crossing the yard at once — piglets, ducklings, a bewildered calf, three baby goats using a sleeping sheep as a climbing structure, two kittens riding the sheep's back like tiny stoic jockeys, chicks scattering underfoot, a rooster supervising with great self-importance, and a single bunny who appears to be leading the whole operation with zero explanation.

Feeding time has devolved magnificently — a calf nuzzling someone's elbow, five piglets spinning in excited circles, four lambs shoving gently from every angle, two puppies skidding through the whole scene, a cluster of chicks riding a piglet like a very slow carousel, kittens dangling from hay bales overhead, two ducklings standing in the water bucket looking pleased, and a goat kid standing on the tallest available surface surveying the chaos as though it planned all of this.
A single speckled duckling waddles across a mossy stone path, pausing to tilt its head at a passing beetle, utterly convinced it has discovered something of great importance.
A sleepy farm cat dozes on a sun-warmed windowsill, one paw dangling lazily over the edge, occasionally cracking one golden eye open to survey the yard with supreme, drowsy authority.

Three fluffy chicks and two fuzzy baby rabbits share a patch of clover in the afternoon light — the chicks pecking boldly while the bunnies twitch their noses and inch closer, both sides pretending they aren't deeply curious about the other.

A wobbly-legged calf and two lambs have wandered into the kitchen garden, the calf gently mouthing a cabbage leaf with wide innocent eyes while the lambs hop sideways through the herb bed, absolutely delighted with themselves.

A whole tumbling crowd of piglets — six of them — spills out from behind the barn, snuffling through the grass in every direction, bumping into each other, reversing, bumping again, one persistently trying to climb over a sibling who has simply sat down and given up.

A fluffy-eared baby goat stands on its hind legs to peer through the cottage window, front hooves on the sill, breath fogging the glass, while two kittens inside press their noses to the pane from the other side in a mutual staring contest nobody is willing to lose.

Seven ducklings trail their mother across the yard in a loose, wobbly line that keeps dissolving — two veer off toward a puddle, one sits down abruptly, another sprints to catch up, and the whole procession collapses into cheerful quacking chaos before somehow reassembling.

An improbable crowd of farm animals has gathered at the back door for no clear reason — four piglets, a pair of lambs, three chicks riding confidently on the back of a patient old sheepdog, two kittens weaving between everyone's legs, a baby goat balanced on the fence post above it all, and one extremely smug rooster overseeing the entire spectacle from the gatepost as if he called this meeting.

A fuzzy brown pony stands at the center of a small admiring huddle — two calves leaning their heavy heads against its flank, a lamb nestled between its front hooves fast asleep, and three chicks perched in a row along its broad back while the pony sighs contentedly and doesn't move an inch.

The feeding-time bell has apparently rung for every creature on the property simultaneously — two geese honking at the front, a stampede of piglets behind them, four lambs bouncing sideways, a litter of puppies tumbling over their own ears, ducklings streaming between everyone's feet, a pair of kittens sprinting along the top of the fence for a better view, and one very startled bunny who got caught in the middle and is now just going with it.
A single sleepy calf curled up in a nest of golden hay, its big dark eyes blinking slowly, one velvet ear twitching at a passing butterfly it is too drowsy to chase.
Two fluffy bunnies nose-to-nose in a patch of clover, one bold and sniffing everything within reach, the other shy and pressed close to the ground, ears flat and eyes wide with cautious wonder.

Three baby goats bouncing across a mossy stone wall in a row, each one leaping off the edge and landing with a joyful stumble, immediately scrambling back up to do it all over again with boundless, giggling energy.

A fluffy farm cat stretched luxuriously across a sunny windowsill with two tiny kittens tumbling across her back, one batting at her tail while the other has already fallen asleep wedged under her chin, both completely unbothered by their mother's resigned expression.

Four ducklings waddling in a determined single-file line through a cottage garden, pausing as a group to peer curiously under each lavender bush, their little tail feathers wiggling with the effort of investigation.

A woolly ewe standing patiently in the afternoon shade while six lambs tumble and bounce around her in every direction, two napping against her sides, one attempting to climb her back, and three chasing each other in dizzy circles through the tall grass.

Seven chicks spilling out of a wooden coop at dawn in a golden flurry, scattering across the yard as a gentle rooster paces behind them like a flustered schoolteacher trying to keep the group together, failing entirely.

A shaggy farm dog trotting through the meadow with six puppies strung out behind in a wiggly parade, each one distracted by something different — a fallen leaf, a mud puddle, a startled grasshopper — while their mother looks back with the exhausted patience of someone who has accepted her fate.

An improbable gathering at the kitchen garden gate: two piglets rooting under the fence, three chicks perched on a sleeping goat, a duckling sitting stubbornly in a watering can, two lambs pressing their noses against the cottage window, a kitten riding on the back of a very tolerant calf, and a puppy spinning in circles having the time of its life for absolutely no reason anyone can determine.

Feeding time has devolved beautifully: a dozen creatures converging from all directions — four ducklings waddling fast, two baby goats already climbing the feed bucket, three piglets squealing with delight, a pair of kittens weaving dangerously between everyone's legs, a bewildered calf standing in the middle of it all, and one very smug rooster surveying the mayhem from atop the fence post as though he planned the whole thing.
A single sleepy calf curled up in a pile of golden hay, its big brown eyes blinking slowly, one velvet ear twitching at a passing fly, completely unbothered and perfectly content.
Two tiny kittens pressed nose-to-nose on a sunny windowsill, one batting lazily at a dangling piece of straw while the other watches with enormous, suspicious eyes before suddenly pouncing.
Three fluffy ducklings waddling single-file through a cottage garden, peeping softly and veering dramatically off course every time a bumblebee floats past, bumping into each other at every turn.
A small gang of four piglets rooting cheerfully through a muddy patch near the fence, their curly tails spinning with excitement, one boldly nosing into a rubber boot left by the gate.

Five baby goats bouncing around a low stone wall — leaping on top, tumbling off, then scrambling back up again — their little hooves click-clacking, eyes bright and absolutely delighted with themselves.

A lively cluster of seven animals gathered at feeding time: three spotted piglets jostling at the trough, two lambs pressing in from the sides, a wobbly calf peering over everyone's shoulders, and one very opinionated duckling standing on the rim quacking instructions at no one in particular.

Six golden chicks racing across the yard in a frantic, chirping blur, chasing the same cabbage butterfly in completely different directions, their tiny legs an absolute flurry, occasionally tripping over each other in delightful slow-motion pileups.

Eight animals lounging in the afternoon shade of a sprawling oak: two puppies tussling over a stick, three lambs flopped against each other in a woolly heap, a farm cat stretching luxuriously across a fence post, and two bunnies sitting perfectly upright with their noses twitching, watching the puppies with calm, aristocratic disapproval.

An absolute farmyard menagerie has assembled with no clear explanation — four piglets, three ducklings, two bouncing baby goats, a pair of kittens riding determinedly on the back of a very patient calf, one rooster strutting through it all like he organized the event, and a sheepdog puppy spinning in joyful circles on the perimeter, contributing nothing useful but tremendous enthusiasm.

Twelve creatures have invaded the vegetable garden and nobody is stopping them: five chicks pecking at strawberries, two lambs wearing lettuce on their heads, three ducklings splashing in an upturned watering can, a piglet sitting squarely in the tomato bed looking enormously pleased, and one bewildered bunny sitting apart from the chaos, staring into the middle distance as if reconsidering all of its life choices.
A single drowsy calf curled up in a patch of afternoon sun, chin resting on folded legs, blinking slowly at nothing in particular, its tufted tail giving the occasional lazy swish.

Two fluffy bunnies pressed side by side in the clover, noses twitching in sync, one bold enough to hop a half-step closer while the other watches from behind a dandelion, whiskers aquiver with shy curiosity.

Three ducklings waddling in an earnest single-file line through the vegetable garden, the leader steering confidently into a cabbage leaf, the two behind piling softly into each other, all three shaking themselves off and carrying on without complaint.

A plump tabby farm cat stretched across a sun-warmed fence post while four chicks mill beneath her, pecking at her dangling tail tip every time it twitches, which she tolerates with the weary dignity of someone who has seen everything.

Five piglets clustered at the edge of a mud puddle, the bravest one belly-deep and squealing with glee, two more edging in cautiously, and the last two watching from dry land with an expression of profound moral conflict.

A rambling cluster of six lambs playing king-of-the-hill on a mossy stone wall, taking turns leaping up, wobbling, and tumbling off into the grass with springy little bounces, each landing provoking a fresh round of enthusiastic head-butting and re-climbing.

Seven animals gathered at the cottage window at dusk — a pair of baby goats standing on their hind legs with hooves on the sill, three chicks perched on the goats' backs, a round puppy pressed against the glass with its nose smooshed flat, and one disapproving rooster supervising from the flower box.

Eight ducklings and two goslings streaming across the yard in a cheerful, honking river, chasing the same cabbage-white butterfly in loose formation, veering left as a unit when it veers left, utterly committed to a mission that has no possible successful outcome.

An inexplicable congregation of twelve animals — four piglets rooting through the herb pots, two kittens dangling from the laundry line, a wobbly calf following a farm dog who is following a goat who is eating the welcome mat, three chicks riding the calf's back by accident, and a single goose honking instructions that absolutely no one is following.

Thirteen animals somehow all in the kitchen garden at once — six ducklings, two lambs, a puppy, three baby rabbits, and one extremely self-satisfied goat standing directly in the center of the strawberry patch — a small chaos ecosystem that has elected itself permanent resident, shuffling and tumbling and nuzzling through every planted row with cheerful, total disregard for the concept of boundaries.
A single drowsy calf curled up in a patch of afternoon sunlight, its big brown eyes blinking slowly, too comfortable to move, one velvet ear twitching at a passing butterfly.
Two fluffy bunnies pressed nose-to-nose in the clover, one bold and curious, sniffing everything within reach, the other shyly peeking out from behind a garden pot before dashing back into hiding.

Three piglets rooting cheerfully through a muddy patch near the fence, jostling each other out of the way with gleeful stubbornness, their curly tails spinning as they discover something buried and utterly fascinating.

A mother duck leading four fuzzy ducklings single-file across the cobblestone path, the last one perpetually distracted, veering off to peck at a daisy before scrambling to catch up with comical urgency.

A round, sleepy farm cat stretched across the top of a fence post while two kittens below take turns batting at her dangling tail, entirely unbothered, radiating the energy of someone who has simply given up.
